verdict.label: Refuted

This rests on well-established background knowledge rather than a retrieved source, since I had no web access, so I am not fully certain of exact dates. Confidence is high because the timeline is well documented.
verdict.explanation: The claim is dated 10 May 2019, but COVID-19 was not identified or named until after that (the virus emerged in Wuhan in late 2019 and the WHO named the disease in February 2020). A COVID-19 fatality rate for Scotland or Italy therefore could not have existed on that date. The 13.9% figure is also not an established value for Italy's COVID-19 fatality rate, which varied over 2020 and depended on how it was measured.
verdict.corrected_claim: COVID-19 did not exist in May 2019: the virus was first identified in late 2019 and the disease was named in February 2020. Any statement about a COVID-19 fatality rate in Scotland or Italy is only meaningful from 2020 onward, and the reported figures changed over time and depended on testing and method.
verdict.correction_reasoning: Based on background knowledge of the COVID-19 timeline (virus identified late 2019, named by WHO 11 Feb 2020). I could not verify current figures offline, so I do not assert the exact Scotland or Italy rates.
